questions.subject: ANALYTICAL_CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: explain the sensitivity of fluorescence
questions.stem: Sample 2901: Why is fluorescence often more sensitive than absorbance spectroscopy?

options.text: Because fluorescence does not require any excitation light source
options.misconception: misstates the need for excitation

options.text: Because emitted light always has a shorter wavelength than excitation
options.misconception: mistakes the Stokes shift for a sensitivity mechanism

options.text: Because emitted light is measured against a nearly dark background rather than a bright incident beam
Because fluorescent molecules have larger molar masses
options.misconception: confuses sensitivity with molecular size

questions.explanation: In fluorescence the detector measures emitted photons at a different wavelength and roughly ninety degrees to the excitation beam, so the background is very low and small signals stand out. Absorbance instead measures a small decrease in a large incident beam.
questions.hint: Think about signal measured against background.

questions.subject: ANALYTICAL_CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: explain the use of line sources in atomic absorption
questions.stem: Sample 2902: In atomic absorption spectroscopy, why is a line source such as a hollow cathode lamp used rather than a continuum source?

options.text: Because atoms absorb light only at visible wavelengths
options.misconception: mistakes the line-source rationale for a wavelength limitation

options.text: Because the lamp also serves as the detector
options.misconception: confuses the source with the detection system

options.text: Because atomic absorption lines are extremely narrow and a line source matches them for sensitive measurement
Because continuum sources cannot produce ultraviolet light at all
options.misconception: misstates the spectral range of continuum lamps

questions.explanation: Free atoms absorb over very narrow wavelength intervals, so a narrow line source whose emission overlaps the atomic transition gives strong, selective absorption. A continuum source would deliver most of its light outside the narrow absorbing window.
questions.hint: Atomic lines are very narrow.
